discernible

/dih-SUR-nuh-buhl/ - the stress falls on SUR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Discernible means able to be seen, noticed, or distinguished.

Once the holiday spikes were stripped out, a slow discernible drift upward ran through five years of the shop's sales figures.

Worked Example

Under raking light, the conservator saw what the gallery's visitors never had: beneath the merchant's black coat, the ghost of an earlier collar, a first attempt the painter had buried. The pentimento was faint — a ridge of paint no thicker than a hair — but under that angled lamp it was discernible, and once seen it could not be unseen.

Discernible is the exact word because the buried collar is able to be seen, noticed, or distinguished — but only just, and only by attention. The word lives in that middle zone: past invisible, well short of obvious. If a thing announces itself from across the room, you don't need discernible; if no effort can find it, the word no longer applies.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

noticeable: Noticeable means a thing draws attention on its own — it flags you down unasked. Discernible is quieter: the detail is genuinely there, but attention has to go looking for it, and a casual glance slides past. Noticeable things interrupt you; discernible things wait to be found.

perceptible: Perceptible sets the barest threshold: the senses can register it at all, however faintly, even if you cannot say what it is. Discernible claims one step more — not just sensed but made out, distinguished clearly enough to be told apart from everything around it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

invisible: cannot be seen no matter the effort

hidden: kept out of sight, where no one can notice it

Where it sits · how easily it can be spotted — detectable → discernible → unmistakable

detectable vs. discernible: Detectable is the barest rung — a trace an instrument or a lab test can find; discernible means careful attention alone can make it out.

unmistakable vs. discernible: Unmistakable goes past discernible: nothing to make out, no attention needed — the thing declares itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart

Root — cern

Root — cern: to sift, to separate (Latin cernere)

Suffix — -ible

Suffix — -ible: able to be

Put it together

Put it together: Dis- (apart) + cern- (to sift, separate) + -ible (able to be) = able to be sifted apart. Latin cernere named what a careful eye does with a heap of grain: separate this from that. Something discernible can be sifted out from its background — seen, noticed, distinguished.

Use the root in a new word: certain

Use the root in a new word: certain: After the third experiment agreed with the first two, the result felt certain.

Word Choice

neutral / precise

Discernible is the careful middle of the visibility scale — use it when a thing can be made out but doesn't leap out. Two traps sit beside it: discerning describes the sharp-eyed person, not the thing seen; and this unit's discretion, though it grows from the same Latin root (cernere, to sift), has drifted to a different job entirely — judgment about what to keep private. Shared ancestry, separate careers.
